html:
In the Six-Day War of June 1967, Israel took the West Bank and East Jerusalem from Jordan, the Gaza Strip and the Sinai from Egypt, and the Golan Heights from Syria. Most of these lands have been under Israeli control since.

Sinai was given back to Egypt by 1982 under the Camp David Accords. Israel annexed East Jerusalem and the Golan, steps most of the world does not recognise. From the late 1960s it built Jewish settlements in the occupied lands; by the 2020s about 700,000 settlers lived in the West Bank and East Jerusalem, which most countries consider illegal.

Palestinians there live under military rule. Israel left Gaza in 2005. The occupation led to the First Intifada and remains at the heart of the conflict. See also Oslo Accords.
sum: In the Six-Day War of June 1967, Israel took the West Bank and East Jerusalem from Jordan, the Gaza Strip and the Sinai from Egypt, and the Golan Heights from Syria. Most of these lands have been under Israeli control since.
